errors.means: The CLI has no command by that word; the kit's answer lists the commands and the nearest one.
errors.fix: Run the command line in the answer's fix, or housesitter --help for the list.

doors.when: A quick check from a controller Mac: does the KVM answer, which route reached the sitter, what it last saw.

errors.means: No Mac was named, or the config has no Mac by that name; the message lists the known ones.
errors.fix: Name one of the Macs in the config, or add it first with housesitter adopt.

errors.means: status was given a flag no Housesitter command reads.
errors.fix: Drop the flag; --json and --plain are the ones status reads.

doors.when: When setting up or debugging: the whole picture in one screen, including whether this computer can administer the KVM.

errors.means: The config has no Mac by the name doctor was given; the message lists the known ones.
errors.fix: Name one of the configured Macs, or run doctor with no name for this computer's own setup.

doors.when: To save the current frame to a file you can open, or to fix the pixel space later clicks use.

errors.means: No route reached the KVM (no endpoint answered and no outbox), or kvmd's snapshot wasn't a usable picture.
errors.fix: Check the KVM is on the network with housesitter status, then take the screenshot again.

errors.means: The config has no Mac by the name screenshot was given.
errors.fix: Name one of the Macs the message lists.

doors.when: From a controller Mac, to press at a point read off the last saved screenshot, right or double with a flag.

errors.means: click acts where other people see it, so it needs --why naming who asked and what they said.
errors.fix: Add --why "<who asked, and what they said>", or --dry-run to see what it would do.

errors.means: x or y isn't a number, or the point is outside the picture housesitter screenshot takes.
errors.fix: Take a screenshot and pass a point inside its width and height, in its pixels.

errors.means: No route reached the Mac's KVM, directly or through the outbox.
errors.fix: Check the KVM with housesitter status, then click again.

errors.means: Through the outbox, the sitter refused the click: the screen isn't a desktop.
errors.fix: Unlock first with housesitter unlock, then click again.

doors.when: From a controller Mac, to send plain words as keystrokes into the field that has focus.

errors.means: type acts where other people see it, so it needs --why naming who asked and what they said.
errors.fix: Add --why "<who asked, and what they said>".

errors.means: The text is empty, over 2000 characters, or looks like a password or token, which the sitter types itself.
errors.fix: Send 1 to 2000 characters of ordinary text; for a password, have the sitter type its own copy.

errors.means: No route reached the Mac's KVM, directly or through the outbox.
errors.fix: Check the KVM with housesitter status, then type again.

errors.means: Through the outbox, the sitter refused: the screen isn't a desktop.
errors.fix: Unlock first with housesitter unlock, then type again.

doors.when: From a controller Mac, to press one key or shortcut, like Return or cmd+tab, through the KVM's keyboard.

errors.means: key acts where other people see it, so it needs --why naming who asked and what they said.
errors.fix: Add --why "<who asked, and what they said>".

errors.means: The combo names a key Housesitter doesn't know.
errors.fix: Write keys joined by +, such as cmd+space or Return.

errors.means: No route reached the Mac's KVM, directly or through the outbox.
errors.fix: Check the KVM with housesitter status, then press again.

errors.means: Through the outbox, the sitter refused the key: the screen isn't a desktop.
errors.fix: Unlock first with housesitter unlock, then press again.

doors.when: From a controller Mac, to move a page or list up or down by a few notches.

errors.means: scroll acts where other people see it, so it needs --why naming who asked and what they said.
errors.fix: Add --why "<who asked, and what they said>".

errors.means: The direction isn't up, down, left or right.
errors.fix: Pass up or down, then how many notches (1 to 20, default 3).

errors.means: No route reached the Mac's KVM, directly or through the outbox.
errors.fix: Check the KVM with housesitter status, then scroll again.

doors.when: When an agent speaks Anthropic's computer-use actions and wants one passed through to the Mac as JSON.

errors.means: computer acts where other people see it, so it needs --why naming who asked and what they said.
errors.fix: Add --why "<who asked, and what they said>".

errors.means: The action isn't one Housesitter runs, or over the outbox it is direct-only (mouse_move, press-and-hold); available lists the ones that work.
errors.fix: Use one of the actions in available.

errors.means: A click action came without coordinate, or the point is off the last screenshot.
errors.fix: Pass coordinate as [x, y] inside the last screenshot.

errors.means: No route reached the KVM, or the action's JSON couldn't be read.
errors.fix: Pass one JSON object, and check the KVM with housesitter status.

doors.when: From a controller Mac, when the screen is at FileVault or a lock screen and its owner wants it opened.

errors.means: unlock acts where other people see it, so it needs --why naming who asked and what they said.
errors.fix: Add --why "<who asked, and what they said>".

errors.means: No route reaches the Mac's sitter, or the sitter won't unlock now (setup mode is on).
errors.fix: Set up SSH with housesitter adopt (or --outbox), or turn setup mode off on the KVM.

errors.means: The sitter tried and the desktop didn't come back, or it refused by its own checks; the message says which.
errors.fix: Look at the screen with housesitter screenshot, then decide whether to try again.

errors.means: With --trial or --hold, arming or holding the password trial over SSH failed; the message carries the KVM's answer.
errors.fix: Check that the KVM is reachable with housesitter doctor <mac>, then run it again.

doors.when: From a controller Mac, when the Mac is hung for good and a hard restart through its plug is worth losing unsaved work.

errors.means: power-cycle acts where other people see it, so it needs --why naming who asked and what they said.
errors.fix: Add --why "<who asked, and what they said>".

errors.means: No route reaches the sitter, the sitter has no plug, or setup mode is on.
errors.fix: Adopt a plug with housesitter plug <mac> adopt, set up a route with housesitter adopt, or turn setup mode off.

errors.means: The sitter refused by its own checks (its budget, the Mac looking alive) or the plug failed; the message says which.
errors.fix: If you have looked and want it anyway, run it again with --attended.

doors.when: From a controller Mac, when the Mac is off and should be up, using its plug or button presser.

errors.means: power-on acts where other people see it, so it needs --why naming who asked and what they said.
errors.fix: Add --why "<who asked, and what they said>".

errors.means: No route reaches the sitter, it has no plug or fingerbot, or setup mode is on.
errors.fix: Set up the route or the power device, or turn setup mode off.

errors.means: The sitter refused by its own checks (a button presser sees the Mac on, or it was switched on minutes ago) or the device failed.
errors.fix: Look with housesitter screenshot; leave a running Mac alone.

doors.when: From a controller Mac, before an agent drives the UI for a while, so a lock in the middle gets undone.

errors.means: want-desktop acts where other people see it, so it needs --why naming who asked and what they said.
errors.fix: Add --why "<who asked, and what they said>".

errors.means: No route reaches the sitter, or its config has unlock_lock_screen off, so agents can't ask.
errors.fix: Set unlock_lock_screen to on_request in the sitter's config, or use housesitter unlock yourself.

errors.means: The request stands, but the first unlock try didn't bring the desktop back.
errors.fix: Look with housesitter screenshot, then try again or unlock it yourself.

doors.when: Before a do: lists the Mac as state with the actions it offers right now and each one's JSON input schema.

errors.means: @ouro.bot/hackamore isn't installed here, and ls needs it.
errors.fix: Run npm install in Housesitter's folder, or run it with npx github:ourostack/housesitter.

errors.means: The config has no Mac by the name ls was given.
errors.fix: Name one of the Macs the message lists.

doors.when: After ls, to run exactly one of the actions it listed, with input that fits that action's schema.

errors.means: do acts where other people see it, so it needs --why naming who asked and what they said.
errors.fix: Add --why "<who asked, and what they said>".

errors.means: That action isn't available on the Mac right now; available lists the ones that are.
errors.fix: Run housesitter ls and pick one of its actions.

errors.means: The input doesn't fit the action's schema; path names the field.
errors.fix: Fix the field at path, using the schema ls shows.

errors.means: The action ran and failed, or @ouro.bot/hackamore isn't installed here.
errors.fix: Read the message; run npm install in Housesitter's folder if hackamore is missing.

doors.when: To compare all Macs at once: last report, staleness and free disk, healthy or not per row.

errors.means: The fleet gist couldn't be read: gh isn't signed in, HOUSESITTER_FLEET_GIST is wrong, or the --from file is unreadable.
errors.fix: Check gh auth status and the gist id, or read a saved copy with --from <gist.json>.

doors.when: To have a different Mac carry out one step on its allowlist and report the result back through the gist.

errors.means: fleet run acts on another Mac, so it needs --why naming who asked and what they said, except with --status.
errors.fix: Add --why "<who asked, and what they said>", or read results with --status.

errors.means: The host or step is missing, or --id names no run request in the fleet gist.
errors.fix: Pass both the host and the step, or an --id that --status lists.

errors.means: The fleet gist couldn't be read or written: no GitHub token, or the wrong gist.
errors.fix: Check gh auth status with a token that may write gists, and HOUSESITTER_FLEET_GIST.

doors.when: When putting the KVM on Tailscale: prints an ACL to paste so the KVM can reach nothing on the tailnet.

errors.means: tailnet-policy takes no words after its name.
errors.fix: Run housesitter tailnet-policy alone.

doors.when: To find which release is installed here, such as before filing a bug or after a deploy.

errors.means: version takes no words after its name.
errors.fix: Run housesitter version alone, or housesitter --version.

doors.when: To show someone what Housesitter does without any hardware, from a recorded evening or a rehearsed night.

errors.means: demo takes at most one word, night.
errors.fix: Run housesitter demo, or housesitter demo night.

doors.when: One read-only look over SSH: what the sitter makes of the screen, then the picture.

errors.means: The config has no Mac by the name look was given; the message lists the known ones.
errors.fix: Name one of the Macs in the config.

errors.means: The sitter's look over SSH failed; the message carries the KVM's own answer, or says it did not answer.
errors.fix: Check that the KVM is reachable with housesitter doctor <mac>, then run it again.

doors.when: To wipe the Mac's password, the KVM's admin password and the outbox token from the KVM and stop the sitter, such as when retiring it.

errors.means: forget was run without --yes, or the config has no Mac by that name; it wipes secrets, so it acts on nothing until confirmed.
errors.fix: Run it again with --yes once you mean it.

errors.means: The wipe over SSH failed; the message carries the KVM's answer. Secrets may still be on the KVM.
errors.fix: Check that the KVM is reachable with housesitter doctor <mac>, then run it again.

doors.when: To teach the sitter the password prompt an operator can see on the KVM's own picture, so it types only where a frame matches.

errors.means: The lesson was refused: no --i-see-the-field, --grid with --filevault, --regions missing, malformed or mixed with --grid or --filevault, or --grid without two fractions.
errors.fix: Read the message: it says which flag to add, drop or fix.

errors.means: The lesson over SSH failed; the message carries the KVM's answer.
errors.fix: Check that the KVM is reachable with housesitter doctor <mac>, then run it again.

doors.when: To check the owner's phone alert works: one real stuck message through the notify rules, marked TEST.

errors.means: alert-test sends a real message to a person, so it needs --why naming who asked and what they said.
errors.fix: Add --why "<who asked, and what they said>", or --dry-run to see who would get it.

errors.means: The sitter couldn't be reached over SSH, or it couldn't send through the notify channel; the answer's result says which.
errors.fix: Check the channel with housesitter doctor <mac>, then run it again.
